headline: Your lungs automatically breathe 20,000 times a day—awake, asleep, without a thought
universal_truth: The body carries us through life while we focus on living it
fun_facts: Your lungs have a surface area of about 70 square meters—half a tennis court, folded inside your chest
You breathe about 20,000 times per day, moving 11,000 liters of air
Unlike the heart, you can consciously override breathing—but only temporarily
discussion_questions: Why do you think breathing can be both automatic and voluntary?
How does conscious breathing change how you feel?
What would life be like if you had to think about every breath?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You've been breathing since birth without thinking about it. Asleep, distracted, unconscious—your lungs keep working. Right now, 300 million tiny air sacs are exchanging oxygen for carbon dioxide. Breathing happens whether you participate or not.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Breathing is automatic, yet you can also control it—hold your breath, breathe faster, breathe slower. No other automatic function gives you this override capability. Why can you control breathing when you can't control your heartbeat?
cliff.prompt: Why can we consciously control breathing but not heartbeat?

options.text: Breathing serves both automatic survival and voluntary functions like speaking and singing
options.response: Yes. We needed conscious breath control for speech, diving, and blowing. The heart needed no such flexibility.

options.text: Breathing is controlled by a different part of the brain than heartbeat
options.response: Different brain regions are involved, but the reason is functional...

q1.title: Folded Surface
q1.script: Your lungs contain about 300 million alveoli—tiny air sacs where gas exchange happens. Unfold them and they'd cover half a tennis court. This enormous surface is crammed into your chest, maximizing contact between air and blood.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Folded Surface"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: 20,000 Breaths
q2.script: You breathe about 20,000 times per day—that's 7.3 million breaths per year. Each breath pulls oxygen in and pushes carbon dioxide out. You never have to remember; your brainstem handles it even when you're unconscious.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Dual Control
q3.script: Breathing is unique: controlled automatically by the brainstem but overridable by conscious thought. This dual control evolved because we needed voluntary breath control for speaking, swimming, and exertion. You can hold your breath—until you can't.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The body carries us while we focus on living. Your lungs breathe whether you're thinking about it or not. Thank your body for handling survival so you can handle everything else.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 88. Tomorrow, we'll explore your body's framework—the skeleton. Until then, take a deep conscious breath—and appreciate the 20,000 you won't have to think about today.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Breath Bridge - Connect Automatic and Conscious
growTrack.learning_objective: Use breath as a bridge between automatic and conscious systems
growTrack.activity: Take five slow, deep breaths. Notice how conscious breathing affects your state—calming, centering, grounding. Breath is unique: an automatic system you can consciously influence. Use this bridge when you need to shift your internal state.
